Who the videos are for

Four owners. Four reasons to reach out.

1

The heir

Inherited minerals from a parent or grandparent, often lives states away, and isn't sure what they own.

"I inherited mineral rights. Now what?"
2

The shrinking check

Royalties used to be steady and keep getting smaller. Wants to know why, and what's coming.

"Why is my royalty check getting smaller?"
3

The offer stack

Gets letters and calls all the time and doesn't know which offers are fair, or who to trust.

"Is this offer any good?"
4

The steward

A family trust, church or nonprofit that was given minerals and needs to manage them well.

"How do we manage a gift like this?"

Every one of them is already asking these questions on Google, YouTube and AI tools like ChatGPT. We make sure Blue Flame is the answer they find.

07
These come straight from your owner stories. The heir, like Scott and Susie or Nancy, who inherited and lives far from the minerals. The shrinking check, whose royalties keep dropping, which is common in the Fayetteville Shale. The offer stack, like George, who had offers but none that made sense. And the steward, like Shodair Children's Hospital, an organization that received minerals as gifts. Each one has a question they're already searching. Each question becomes a high trust video.

12
[Click 1: captions and questions. Click 2: same words, where AI looks. Click 3: monthly check.] There are two halves to this. Step one is claiming Blue Flame in ChatGPT's business hub, so the AI has your name, address, basins and services right. We'll do that in week one. But that's you describing you, and every competitor can do the same. What moves the answer is other people talking about you. One: creators say your name on camera, and captions, titles and descriptions turn that into text the AI reads. Two: every video answers a question owners actually type. Three: many different voices, heirs, basin-town creators, attorneys, CPAs, use the same phrases, so the AI connects those questions to Blue Flame. Four: it's posted where AI looks, YouTube, podcasts, local news, professional blogs, forums and reviews, linking back to the check-up page. Five: every month we ask the major AI tools the same 25 owner questions and report how often you're named. We can't control what an AI says, but we can make Blue Flame the name that keeps coming up.

13
QLC, Qualified Lead Count: owners with minerals in the Fayetteville Shale or the Bakken who asked for a check-up. Your land team confirms the ownership. CPL: what each of those owners cost to bring in. The most useful comparison is with what an outbound conversation costs you today in specialist hours, lists and mail. At kickoff we agree the basins and counties, what counts as qualified and booked, and which lists we're allowed to use. On top of those two numbers, we report a monthly AI check: we ask ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity and Google the same 25 owner questions and track how often Blue Flame gets named. That number should climb as creator videos and professional content build up.

Connect and Align

Outbound doesn't disappear

Keep the phones. Change who's on the other end.

A specialist's day today
  1. Pull a list from county records
  2. Dial, leave a voicemail, dial again
  3. Explain who Blue Flame is to someone who's heard it before
  4. Most calls end before the process starts
With the inbound engine
  1. Start with owners who asked for a check-up
  2. Then call owners on your lists, after weeks of seeing Blue Flame stories
  3. Cold dials last, and fewer of them
  4. More calls start at Connect and Align

Same team, same process. Less time chasing, more time with owners who want the help.

16
[Click 1: the new day. Click 2: the takeaway.] We're not asking you to fire the phones. Your specialists are good on the phone; that's why your reviews mention them by name. We're changing the order of their day. First, owners who asked for a check-up. Then owners on your lists, who by now have been seeing Blue Flame stories for weeks, so the call isn't cold anymore. Cold dials last, and fewer of them. The platforms show counts, not which individual watched, so the warm-up is about timing, not surveillance.
